frontier.hypothesis: Target's loop-2 preheader copy is emitted by a pass that runs AFTER cse and combine - loop.c's strength-reduction preheader emission (emit_iv_add_mult) or regmove.c - and therefore has no C-level handle at all. This is s13's frontier item #2, still the sharpest live statement of the wall, and it remains untouched by any session: s14 spent its budget on the TU axis and on permuter breadth instead.
frontier.mechanism: Both of target's preheaders end with `addu v0,a0,v1` (the strength-reduced giv init for `base + i`), which is loop.c output emitted into the preheader after cse/combine have run. s10 proved loop 2's guard block is a JOIN with two predecessors (loop 1's skip branch `blez $v0,.L8001791C` lands on it, asm/funcs/func_80017848.s:62) so cse's extended basic block provably cannot reach loop 2's preheader - meaning loop 2's copy cannot be a cse fold the way loop 1's is. s14 adds two independent confirmations that no C-level spelling reaches it: a directed cross-product over every ledger-3 lever, and a whole-function randomizer seeded on a non-V1 chassis.
frontier.next_probe: Generate the full cc1 -da dump series for the V1 chassis using the re-pathed tmp/grind/func_80017848/s10/dump.sh and walk the loop-2 preheader insn stream ACROSS passes: .cse -> .loop -> .combine -> .lreg -> .greg. Identify at which dump the `addu a3,a0,zero`-shaped copy would have to appear, and in the .loop dump compare loop 1's and loop 2's giv/biv records side by side - they differ in OUTCOME inside a single dump, so the deciding record is directly visible. Do NOT re-probe any preheader addend spelling, declaration order, parameter homing, loop-body spelling, exit form, loop shape, base-destination local, or TU context: all measured dead by s11/s12 (hand), s13/s14 (machine) and s14 (TU).

frontier.hypothesis: The residual is decided by local-alloc's allocno ORDERING, which is driven by reg_n_refs - the raw reference COUNT of the ctx+0xC pointer pseudo - and that count can be moved from C without changing any statement's meaning, by varying how many times ctx+0xC is read in the TAIL (which target itself reads three separate times).
frontier.mechanism: The three residual instructions are a straight SWAP of `lw a0,12(s2)` and `move a3,a0` between loop 1's exit tail and loop 2's preheader, i.e. a tie broken the other way, not a missing computation. local-alloc orders allocnos by priority computed from reg_n_refs and live length, so changing the number of references to the pointer pseudo is the one input to that ordering still reachable from C. s11 measured routing tail reads THROUGH a live local (19 points) but never measured varying the NUMBER of independent fresh reads in the tail, which is a duplicate-read spelling rather than a lifetime change.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep the tail's ctx+0xC read count on the V1 chassis with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s13/score.sh: target reads it three times (math_Distance3D's two arguments share one read, then rec_a, then rec_b). Cells: (a) one fresh read per math_Distance3D argument (4 reads total); (b) rec_a and rec_b sharing one read (2 reads); (c) each of the four sites reading freshly; (d) the same sweep on the ctx+0x10 links pointer. Each cell is a pure duplicate-read respelling in the sanctioned family - no dead locals, no unused declarations (see rejected/unused_local_decl_q_contaminates_sweeps.c for why an unused decl invalidates a sweep).

frontier.hypothesis: Instrumented cc1 can answer directly what six sessions have inferred: which pass materialises loop 1's preheader copy but not loop 2's, and what the deciding predicate is.
frontier.mechanism: The instrumented cc1 with the BB2_*_DEBUG hooks is tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 (NOT tools/gcc-2.7.2/build/cc1 - three grind sessions have already lost time to that, see the instrumented-cc1-location memory). It can print cse's hash-table hits, can_combine_p refusals and local-alloc's combine_regs decisions at named insns, which converts every 'the copy must come from pass X' inference in s6-s13 into a measurement.
frontier.next_probe: Compile the V1 chassis with tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 under the BB2_*_DEBUG hooks and capture, for the two preheader blocks specifically: (1) whether cse records a hash entry for the ctx+0xC load in each block, (2) every can_combine_p refusal touching the copy insn, (3) local-alloc's combine_regs tie decisions for the base-add pseudo in each loop. Diff the two blocks' traces - the first divergence IS the answer. Save the traces under tmp/grind/func_80017848/s15/ and list them as artifacts.
